items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: I don’t know whether Roy and Ben Webster — Roy Eldridge and Ben Webster — were on that band or not, because I didn’t know at that time.

ctx.x: Okay. It was kind of like by recommendation that they would let you in.

Yes. Uh huh. And anyhow but in the meantime I’m down there watching all the drummers. Every time something would happen — as a matter of fact, going way back, before I became interested, back in the early thirties, it was during the depression, and not only did we have the Music Project but you had another project where they would send people, show business people, people that had stage experience, and they would send them around to the neighborhoods and I remember the house, there was a house on Sacramento…

then there would be a dance after that. So we did our skit and then the band, they were already set up and they came from the dressing room or wherever they were and they started to play for the dancing. It turned out to be the Fletcher Henderson orchestra. And now what am I, twelve years old? Thirteen years old? Something like that. Here’s the Fletcher Henderson orchestra. Now the drummer’s name was Pete Suggs — S-U-G-G-S. And I’ve seen his name on some of the personnel on some of the older records now. I don’t…
